title: What If Our Sun Were a Red Dwarf Instead?

scenes.text: What if our Sun were a red dwarf, the galaxy's most common star? Earth would have to move.
About three-quarters of the Milky Way's stars are red dwarfs, and most shine at less than a tenth of the Sun's light.
To stay warm, Earth would need an orbit inside Mercury's, and its year would last somewhere between 3 and 150 days.
Tidal forces would likely lock one side toward the star forever: permanent day on one side, permanent night on the other.
Red dwarfs also flare, doubling their brightness within minutes, and the worst flaring may last the star's first 1.2 billion years.
The upside: a small red dwarf can burn for up to about 10 trillion years, a thousand times longer than our Sun's ten billion.

description:
What if our Sun were a red dwarf?
Earth would need an orbit inside Mercury's and a year of just days, but the star could shine for trillions of years.
